scope: Complete static reading of acquisition contract, current collector, and full-code-read receipt only. No collector or prior helper execution, no network, no source content inspection, no paper-directory writes.

findings.title: Filesystem-alias collisions can merge distinct native directory members
findings.mechanism: Preflight seen-set compares case-sensitive normalized POSIX strings only. On a case-insensitive filesystem, distinct members A/ and a/ pass preflight but mkdir(exist_ok=True) resolves them to the same directory. Likewise canonically equivalent Unicode spellings can alias on some macOS filesystems. A successful final manifest can therefore contain fewer distinct directories than the native ZIP topology while member metadata lists both.
findings.condition: Requires an archive with aliased names and a filesystem on which those names identify the same object; no claim about the actual two unopened archives is made.
findings.recommended_correction: Reject filesystem-alias paths during preflight or validate that every distinct normalized member resolves to a distinct extraction location; fail before closure if topology cannot be represented faithfully.

findings.title: Directory-entry payloads are accepted without custody hashing
findings.mechanism: item.is_dir() depends on a trailing slash. No preflight assertion requires directory-member file_size to be zero. An entry named a/ with nonzero payload is recorded as native_uncompressed_bytes > 0, but extraction never reads the member, never checks its data CRC, and reports extracted_bytes=0. The outer ZIP is preserved, yet the claimed all-member extraction and per-member payload custody are incomplete for that accepted input.
findings.condition: Requires a ZIP directory entry with nonzero data; no claim about the actual two unopened archives is made.
findings.recommended_correction: Fail closed if a directory member has nonzero uncompressed bytes, or explicitly preserve and hash the directory member data as a separate byte object.

successful_static_checks: Collector performs ordinary public GETs and does not contain source/program execution or mathematical text extraction.
Existing sources are checked and fresh directory creation is exclusive; source-file writes use exclusive creation.
Raw API JSON and record-page bytes, native full file entries and order, native MD5 literals, and independently computed length/MD5/SHA256 are preserved.
Path traversal, absolute paths, links, special entries, encryption and exact normalized duplicate ZIP members are rejected.
Complete filesystem enumeration ignores no dotfile or ignore patterns, records empty directories and effective permission modes.
Native ZIP member attributes/order and archive bytes remain separately pinned.
Outer paper.pdf identity is separate from every embedded PDF location/digest without mathematical content classification.
Manifest covers finite payload excluding two declared control files, final binds manifest, and lane external pins bind both without hash circularity.
limitations: This is a static collector audit, not runtime or actual-archive verification.

On a partial two-record failure, the first record can have a completed SOURCE_FINAL before EXTERNAL_SOURCE_PINS is written at the end; the run must be reported incomplete and the already-created source folders must not be overwritten.
Initial URLs are restricted to zenodo.org; redirect destinations are recorded but not restricted before following.
Immutability is procedural; the collector does not apply OS-level immutable flags or remove write permission.
follow_up: Parent decides and performs any correction; auditor will not execute collector or mutate acquisition sources.
